♡Family Today♡

Luka has the cover, zipped into the planets and rockets and almost ready for bed. One more mild day, then the rain arrives: a few showers late tonight, the real soaking Thursday night and Friday, and a sunny, cooler weekend behind it. Last day of September.
  • Oct 4Patriots at Buffalo, Jets at Chicago — both 1:00
  • Oct 4Las Vegas, NASCAR playoffs — 5:30, USA
  • Oct 23Claire's birthday
  • Oct 25Garret and Ariel's birthday
  • Nov 3Election Day
Had a migraine? Say so in the group chat — the day and roughly when — and the paper will mark it on the Barograph. Enough entries and we will know what the glass does before one hits.

Aries
The moon sextiles Mars today, an easy link between feeling and doing. Whatever you have been putting off moves more easily than it did on Monday. Kaylani, Luka
Cancer
The moon is at the last degree of Taurus, steady ground before it turns restless in Gemini tonight. Get the practical thing done while the day is still calm. Gregg
Leo
Mercury, just into Scorpio, squares Mars in your sign. Someone will say exactly what they think. Hear the useful part and let the tone go. Leah, Tommy
Virgo
Your ruler, Mercury, crossed into Scorpio this morning and squares Pluto. Conversations go deeper than planned. Ask the second question. Derek, Joanne
Scorpio
Mercury is in your sign now, beside Venus. For the next three weeks words come easier and land better. Say the thing you have been rehearsing. Ariel, Claire, Garret

✶The Ledger✶

Inches of rain due Thursday night and Friday
1+
A half to three-quarters of an inch Thursday night and as much again Friday, by the Weather Service's count. Enough to soak the lawns and the leaves.

✶The National Wire✶

1

U.S. Forces Leave Iraq

The Pentagon says American troops and equipment are out, 23 years after the invasion, and has declared the anti-ISIS mission over.

2

A.I. Companies Sign a Voluntary Accord

The president said leaders of the major A.I. firms agreed to "self-police," with internal and outside reviews of new systems. It is not a law.

3

FBI Hit by a Data Breach

Hackers got into the bureau's job-applicant portal. The FBI calls the breach massive and says it is going after those responsible.

4

Polo Floods the Southwest

The hurricane's remains flooded roads, and small New Mexico towns evacuated over fears a dam could fail.

☑ The Ballot · 34 days to Election Day · early voting Oct 24–Nov 1 · register by Oct 24

⛪The Home Wire⛪

1

North Tonawanda · LumberJack's Lease Bought Out

The city bought out LumberJack's Patio Grill's lease on its River Road spot and is looking for a new restaurant to open there by next summer.

2

Buffalo · A Two-Year Pause on Data Centers?

City lawmakers moved a step toward a two-year ban on new data centers, double the state's one-year pause already in effect. Not final yet.

3

Henrietta · Federal Money for Four Firefighters

A grant of nearly $1 million will add four firefighters as volunteer ranks thin; eleven Rochester-area departments share more than $2.5 million.

★The Marquee★

1

Backpack Wins Fat Bear Week

Bear 89, "Backpack," beat 910 in the final vote at Alaska's Katmai National Park, the annual online vote for the chunkiest bear.

2

Hanson Hits the End on DWTS

Taylor Hanson was eliminated from Dancing With the Stars after the show's yacht rock night.

3

Tom Cruise's Big Gamble

Digger, his film with Oscar winner Alejandro G. Iñárritu, screened at the Academy Museum; the Hollywood Reporter calls it his riskiest business yet.

🏈The Gridiron🏈

Four Days to Sunday
Bills · Christian Benford left the Chargers game with a toe injury and was in a walking boot afterward; watch Wednesday's practice report. The Patriots come in short-handed, with A.J. Brown on injured reserve and three others hurt.
Jets · Bears quarterback Caleb Williams is out three to four weeks with a hamstring injury, so Case Keenum starts Sunday. Keenum led Monday's 27–7 win over the Eagles, and with Williams out the line has dropped from Chicago by 8½ to 3½.

☾On This Day☾

September 30, 1927 — Babe Ruth hit his 60th home run of the season at Yankee Stadium, a record that stood for 34 years. Baseball's postseason opened this week; the Braves won Tuesday's wild-card opener against the Phillies on a three-run homer in the eighth.
